As of June 2026, there were 17 companies with a market capitalization over $1 trillion, a significant jump from 12 in 2025 [officechai.com]. The discrepancy in earlier reports likely lies in the fluidity of market caps which fluctuate daily [tickerplace.com].

The "trillion-dollar club" is heavily dominated by US technology and semiconductor companies, with only TSMC (Taiwan), Saudi Aramco (Saudi Arabia), and Samsung (South Korea) among the top non-US names [tickerplace.com]. SpaceX notably joined the club in 2026, with its market cap crossing $2.5 trillion within days of its IPO [officechai.com]. Other recent additions or companies that have solidified their trillion-dollar status due to the AI infrastructure boom include NVIDIA, Meta, Broadcom, Micron, and SK Hynix [officechai.com]. SK Hynix and Samsung, two South Korean chipmakers, have seen their combined value surpass China's largest internet companies, Alibaba and Tencent, due to the AI-driven memory chip boom [ibtimes.com.au].

Currently, Eli Lilly ($990 billion) and Walmart ($950 billion) are close to the trillion-dollar mark [visualcapitalist.com]. Meanwhile, SK Hynix and Micron Technology are in the trillion-dollar range, at approximately $1.1+ trillion each. The continued growth largely depends on sustained AI infrastructure spending [officechai.com].

Note: discarded an earlier June 2026 count of 14 companies in favor of the more recent/consistent figure of 17 trillion-dollar companies as of 2026; removed specific valuations for SK Hynix ($1.12T) and Micron ($1.10T) from tickerplace.com as they conflict with the June 2026 baseline and cannot be precisely dated.
research_texts.q_43924:
Between July 20 and September 1, 2026, the Russia-Ukraine war will likely see continued Ukrainian long-range strikes deep into Russia and occupied territories, combined with Russian missile and drone attacks on Ukraine, and limited ground advances.

Ukrainian forces continued their long-range strike campaign on July 24 and 25, hitting a Wildberries warehouse in Yekaterinburg (1,800 km from Ukraine), an oil refinery near Tyumen City (1,980 km from the frontline), and targets in Rostov-on-Don, including an S-400 radar system and fuel depots. Ukrainian forces also struck Caspian Sea assets, including an oil platform, a missile boat, and sanctioned cargo vessels, according to Ukrainian President Zelensky and the SBU [isw.org](https://understandingwar.org/research/russia-ukraine/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-july-25-2026/). Ukraine's deep-strike campaign is becoming more strategically relevant, aiming to strengthen its negotiating position [randforecastinginitiative.org](https://www.randforecastinginitiative.org/question_queue/questions/1784-which-trajectory-will-best-describe-the-russia-ukraine-war-by-september-31-2026).

Russia launched 1,700 drones and 95 missiles this week, striking civilian infrastructure and an agricultural enterprise in Sumy Oblast, and port infrastructure in Mykolaiv Oblast [kyivpost.com](https://www.kyivpost.com/post/81093). Russia is expanding its gasoline export ban until the end of 2026, and a Romanian F-16 intercepted an unidentified drone in Romanian airspace on July 25 [isw.org](https://understandingwar.org/research/russia-ukraine/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-july-25-2026/).

While Russia has ramped up assault groups in July, Russian ground advances have slowed significantly, and neither side made confirmed advances on July 25 [rbc.ua](https://newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/russian-assault-groups-surge-18-in-july-amid-1785053738.html), [isw.org](https://understandingwar.org/research/russia-ukraine/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-july-25-2026/). Russia aims for complete Ukrainian capitulation and has exaggerated its territorial gains, claiming 2,226 square kilometers in the first six months of 2026, while ISW assessed a net gain of 81.1 square kilometers [isw.org](https://understandingwar.org/research/russia-ukraine/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-july-22-2026/).
